short: The Germanic general Odoacer deposed the last western Roman emperor and did not appoint a successor.
full:
On 4 September 476 CE, the Germanic officer Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus, a teenage emperor installed a year earlier by his own father, after Odoacer's troops mutinied over unpaid land grants and turned on the boy's regime. Unlike his predecessors, Odoacer did not proclaim a new emperor in the west; instead he sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople and had himself recognised as king of Italy under the nominal authority of the eastern emperor Zeno.

Contemporaries did not necessarily see the moment as apocalyptic: the western throne had already changed hands rapidly for decades, and a rump of imperial authority persisted a little longer in Gaul under Syagrius. But later historians, beginning with sixth-century writers looking back on a Europe of Germanic kingdoms, fixed on 476 as the conventional end of the western Roman Empire, a date now used as a boundary in most surveys of antiquity.
